findings.F1: The weekend effect is all on Saturday. At Friday's close the 14-day volatility-scaled rise predicts Saturday's excess return with slope 0.0056 (t 2.85, 2118 cases, 363 days). By z14 quintile, from fall to rise, Saturday's excess return is −0.38 %, −0.14 %, +0.32 %, +0.41 % and +1.07 %. It predicts nothing for Sunday (slope t 0.17) or for Monday and Tuesday together (t −0.52).
findings.F2: The Friday-to-Saturday slope holds in both halves of the period: t 2.11 up to 2021 (1056 cases) and t 2.01 from 2022 (1062 cases). It also holds for other lookbacks. Friday's 7-day rise gives t 2.95 and its 28-day rise t 2.68. Thursday's 7-day rise predicts Saturday's return, its day after, with t 3.36.
findings.F3: The same past rise predicts nothing for the next day on any other weekday. The 14-day slope t is −0.54 on Monday bars, −0.13 on Tuesday, −0.11 on Wednesday, 1.29 on Thursday, −0.33 on Saturday and 0.00 on Sunday. The continuation is specific to Saturday, not a general daily trend.
findings.F4: The book earns its weekend on Saturday and takes its tail on Sunday. Its mean daily return is +0.267 % on Saturdays against +0.060 % on Sundays. Of its worst 2 % of active days, 61 fall on Sunday and 31 on Saturday. Of its best 2 %, 55 fall on Saturday and 37 on Sunday.
findings.F5: A large Saturday move partly reverses on Sunday. Saturday's volatility-scaled move predicts Sunday's excess return with slope −0.0052 (t −2.29, 2172 cases). The top Saturday quintile (mean z 1.15) is followed by −0.75 % on Sunday and the bottom quintile (mean z −0.90) by +0.24 %. With more than 50 slopes examined, this is borderline.

ideas.idea: The higher a coin's 14-day rise, measured in its usual daily moves at Friday's close (UTC), the more it rises over the following day, Saturday, alone.
ideas.consequence: A trader would hold a coin long over Saturday after a two-week rise, more firmly the larger the rise, and would not carry the bet into Sunday, which adds the book's deepest falls without adding gain.
ideas.name: two-week rise carries Saturday

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's rise on Saturday (UTC), measured in its usual daily moves, the more it falls back over the following day, Sunday.
ideas.consequence: A trader would refuse to carry a long into Sunday after a strong Saturday, more so the stronger Saturday was, and would lean short against that move for the day.
ideas.name: Saturday surge fades Sunday
